podcast.title: Comparison to Matt Bellamy
podcast.body: She is considered a potential "female equivalent to Mewz's Met Bellamy," suggesting her high caliber as a guitarist and artist. "If there's a female equivalent to Mewz's Met Bellamy, it's probably her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continuous Musical Evolution
podcast.body: St. Vincent, whose real name is Annie Clark, has demonstrated a steady ascent in her career, with her music progressively improving with each album release over the years. "Any Clark, which is St. Vincent's real name, began a slowest scent years ago and has been getting better and better and better with each album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ernie Ball Music Man Signature Guitar – Custom Design
podcast.body: St. Vincent is one of the few guitarists with a custom signature model, the Ernie Ball Music Man St. Vincent Signature Model. Designed based on her 20+ years of playing experience, it is lightweight, comfortable for both standing and sitting, available in various colors, and features three mini humbuckers with a "convoluted but very cool pickup configuration" for extensive tone flexibility. "She is one of the few people who has a custom signature guitar built just for her. It's called the Ernie Ball Music Man St. Vincent Signature Model."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guitar Solo Composition Method
podcast.body: St. Vincent sometimes composes her guitar solos on a MIDI keyboard before meticulously learning and transferring them to be played on her guitar. "Sometimes she works out her solos on a MIDI keyboard and then learns them for the guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Highly Respected by Fellow Guitarists
podcast.body: St. Vincent is highly revered by other guitarists, noted as one of the few, and possibly the only woman, to have her own custom signature guitar model. "She is so revered by other guitarists. She is one of the few people and seriously, the only woman I can think of who has her own custom signature guitar built just for her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Independent Culture Favorite
podcast.body: St. Vincent is recognized as one of those great artists cherished by the independent music culture. "San Vincent a ver yo creo que es una de esas grandes artistas que a toda la cultura independiente le encantan."

podcast.title: Innovative Soloing and Effects Usage
podcast.body: St. Vincent, also known as Annie Clark, approaches soloing by sometimes developing parts on a MIDI keyboard before translating them to guitar. She also employs a collection of fuzz pedals in unique combinations to generate guitar sounds that transcend traditional guitar tones. "Sometimes she works out her solo on a MIDI keyboard and then learns them for guitar. She has a collection of fuzz pedals that she combines in weird ways to make her guitar sound like something other than a guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Modern Guitar Hero
podcast.body: St. Vincent is considered a bona fide modern guitar hero, whose talent and commercial success have played a role in reversing a significant downturn in electric guitar sales in the 21st century. She has achieved such icon status that she has her own signature model electric guitar. "This woman has become such a guitar icon that she has her own signature model. It's St. Vincent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 7: (40-31)

podcast.title: Personal View on "Guitar Hero" Status
podcast.body: Despite her influence and recognition, St. Vincent personally does not identify with the term "guitar hero," finding it a "strange thing," but expresses excitement if she inspires young people to play guitar. "I don't think about that in those terms ever. I really don't. It would be a strange thing for me, like Psychic Lita. ... Great. I'm so excited if kids want to play guitar. It's the best thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signature Guitar's Widespread and Unorthodox Appeal
podcast.body: The Ernie Ball Music Man St. Vincent Signature Model, with its "retro, future" and "unorthodox shape," has garnered appeal across diverse genres. It has been played by notable artists like Jack White (on SNL) and Tom Morello, and even metalheads (via a stealth black version) and country players, highlighting its versatility and unique design. "Jack White played it on SNL. Tom Morello has one. I've seen, we make an all black version. It's like the stealth version, which is for metalheads. And metal dudes play it. There's country players who are playing it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Guitar Sound
podcast.body: She is known for using a distinctive collection of fuzz pedals, which she combines in "weird ways" to make her guitar sound like "something other than a guitar," contributing to her signature sonic palette. "She has a collection of fuzz pedals that she combines in weird ways to make her guitar sound like something other than a guitar."

xref.title: Discharge from St. Vincent's Hospital
xref.body: Shane MacGowan was discharged from St. Vincent's Hospital in Dublin on November 23, 2023, as medical professionals could no longer provide further assistance. "Shane was discharged from St. Vincent's hospital in Dublin on November 23, 2023."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Discovery at King Tuts Wah Wah Hut
xref.body: Oasis was allegedly discovered by Alan McGee of Creation Records at King Tuts Wah Wah Hut on St. Vincent Street in Glasgow, Scotland, on May 31, 1993. This event purportedly occurred after the band threatened the owner with arson if they were not allowed to perform that night. "Oasis was discovered by Alan McGee of creation records after they allegedly threatened the owner with arson if he didn't let them play that night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Juno Awards 50th Anniversary Performance
xref.body: The surviving members of The Tragically Hip reunited to perform at the 50th anniversary of the Juno Awards on June 6th, 2021, with Feist filling in on vocals. There was initial "resistance amongst all of us to delve back in and open that door," but the decision was made due to the significance of the 50th anniversary, the honor being received, and the desire to support musicians and live venues during a period of hardship. Feist was suggested as a singer, and the band felt "everyone had that same response," believing Gordon Downie would approve. The performance was compared to Nirvana's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction performance with female vocalists like Lorde, St. Vincent, Kim Gordon, and Joan Jett. "if there was a time when we were going to entertain the idea that this is probably it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
